children: Gold futures settle modestly higher as the U.S. dollar weakens for a second session, with gains limited by a slight uptick in U.S. yields. Most market participants still expect the Fed to hold rates steady this month, which could provide some relief for gold, DHF Capital's Bas Kooijman says in a note. "However, it could remain vulnerable to downside risks as markets continue to see more tightening in December and beyond." High oil prices keep up risks for inflation and tighter monetary policy, he adds. Front month gold settles up 0.3% in New York at $4,159.50 a troy ounce. Silver also edges up 0.3% to $56.995 a troy ounce. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
